purpose: Route evidence beyond the canonical organizer/Trace manifest. These references may support race-day geometry, historical course reconstruction and source triangulation, but do not automatically assign course versions.
rules: A participant activity is evidence for a race-day recording only when the activity title/date/author can be linked to a known race participation or the activity text explicitly identifies the race.
An activity landing page without exportable coordinates is retained as a reference lead, not a local route asset.
Watch ascent is diagnostic only and must not be mixed directly with standardized cross-year elevation.
Mapped/copy routes are weaker than actual race-day recordings for reconstructing what runners physically followed.
Organizer map images can establish route-shape evidence but do not enable replay or exact distance projection without georeferencing or GPX geometry.

sources.evidence: Current 14 km Race-PM embeds this legacy-labelled organizer map/elevation image. It shows one loop from Christinehof with an eastern out-and-back/loop to the Hallamölla/Verkeån corridor and an approximately 13 km profile.
sources.limitation: The legacy 13 km label means the image alone must not be used to claim exact identity for every trail14 year or exact 2026 distance.

sources.evidence: Current Naturloppet page embeds an organizer map showing the 5 km loop west/north-west of Christinehof in the Ekopark. The image includes SWEREF 99 TM corner coordinates (SW approximately N 6173751 / E 437733; NE approximately N 6176791 / E 442965), a north arrow and scale information, so the published route line is georeferenceable rather than merely schematic.
sources.limitation: The route is still a raster line, not an organizer GPX. Any digitized coordinates must be labelled derived_from_georeferenced_organizer_map and validated against independent race-day GPS before promotion to canonical race-day geometry.

sources.evidence: The separate Jogg GPSPass page proves a GPS registration exists for the race-day activity. The participant text explicitly says ÖST 13+ km and reports her watch at 13.67 km / 1:31:44; Hallamölla is mentioned with 4.5 km remaining.
sources.limitation: Jogg's aggregate page shows 15.55 km / 1:50:06, inconsistent with the participant's explicit race-watch values. Do not use the Jogg aggregate as course distance until the underlying coordinate series/segmentation is acquired and inspected.

sources.evidence: Organizer programme states the 5 km course runs through Ekoparken with the first 3 km on gravel/forest roads and the last 2 km on narrow, fairly technical trails, with stairs on the finishing approach. The 13 km course is described as slightly shorter than 13 km.
sources.limitation: 2021 races were affected by pandemic planning/cancellation context; this is historical course-description evidence, not proof that a race-day recording exists for 2021.

sources.evidence: The organizer's 2022 page states that start times may differ but course routes and other details are the same. Together with the retained historical programme, this supports continuity of the short-course concept around the 2021/2022 configuration.
sources.limitation: The statement does not provide coordinates and is not strong enough by itself to assign exact geometry or prove identity with the current raster.

sources.evidence: Independent contemporary race report confirms Abelone Lyng ran Naturloppet 5 km+ the day after her ÖST Ultra and finished joint second on net time. Bøler IF independently records the same 23:10 result.
sources.limitation: Strong participant/result anchor for result→GPS matching, but no public coordinate series or watch distance was found.
